cases.priority_problem: inferior STEMI with possible right ventricular involvement
cases.patho: inferior myocardial ischemia causing bradycardia, hypotension, and preload sensitivity
cases.trap: Learners may focus on pain only and miss hypotension/bradycardia safety implications.
cases.q3_trap: Reflexively giving nitroglycerin is unsafe in hypotensive/RV infarct patterns.
cases.q4_trap: Not every chest pain medication is safe for every chest pain patient.
cases.q5_trap: Pain relief should not outrank reperfusion and hemodynamic safety.
cases.q6_trap: Symptom improvement does not mean the STEMI resolved.
cases.teach: Inferior STEMI plus hypotension means think RV involvement before nitroglycerin.
cases.safety: Nitroglycerin can worsen hypotension in preload-dependent patients.
cases.q4_safety: Medication contraindication screening is a safety intervention.
cases.q6_teach: Evaluate reperfusion progress, hemodynamics, rhythm, and symptoms.

cases.priority_problem: lithium toxicity worsened by dehydration and renal impairment
cases.patho: narrow-therapeutic-index drug accumulation causing neurologic toxicity and renal clearance risk
cases.trap: GI symptoms can look like a stomach virus, but with lithium they are toxicity warnings.
cases.q3_trap: Psychiatric history can distract learners from medical toxicity.
cases.q4_trap: Continuing scheduled medications can be harmful when toxicity is suspected.
cases.q5_trap: Do not give the next lithium dose because it is due.
cases.q6_trap: A decreasing lithium level can still be toxic.
cases.teach: Lithium has a narrow therapeutic index; dehydration and drug interactions change safety.
cases.safety: Continuing lithium with toxicity can worsen neurologic injury.
cases.q4_safety: Hydrochlorothiazide can worsen lithium toxicity and should be held when toxicity is suspected.
cases.q5_safety: Fall/seizure precautions and monitoring reduce injury while toxicity persists.
cases.q6_teach: Trend direction and absolute value both matter.
cases.q6_safety: Persistent neurologic findings require continued precautions.

notes.note: Vomiting and diarrhea for two days, poor intake, worsening hand tremor, and confusion about medication timing.
Coarse tremor, unsteady gait, slurred responses, and reports taking lithium this morning.
Hold lithium and hydrochlorothiazide. Start isotonic IV fluids, ECG, neurologic monitoring, and fall/seizure precautions.
Lithium held. IV fluids infusing. Fall precautions initiated due to ataxia and confusion.
More alert but tremor and gait instability persist. No seizure activity observed.

orders.order: Hold lithium and hydrochlorothiazide immediately due to suspected toxicity and renal impairment.
Administer 0.9% sodium chloride IV fluids and monitor urine output, neurologic status, and cardiac rhythm.
Implement fall and seizure precautions and notify provider for worsening confusion, seizure, or dysrhythmia.
